description.value: Kwa'lilas Hotel is the only Indigenous-owned 4-star hotel on northern Vancouver Island, located in Port Hardy at the northern tip of the island. Named from the Kwak̓wala word for 'a place to sleep,' it was curated by Gwa'sala-'Nakwaxda'xw Elders and features original Indigenous artwork, masks, and cultural displays throughout. Touring cyclists finishing or beginning the full island route will find on-site dining at Nax'id' Pub and Ha'me' Restaurant, plus modern room amenities in a culturally immersive setting.

address.value: 9040 Granville St, Port Hardy, BC V0N 2P0

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website content is fully available and corroborates all OSM contact fields. The rooms page explicitly confirms complimentary high-speed internet, and the hotel has two on-site food/drink venues (Ha'me' Restaurant and Nax'id' Pub), satisfying 'Nearby evening food'. No mention of bike storage, bike procedures, laundry, e-bike charging, or any other cycling-specific amenities appears anywhere in the website content, so those fields are null.
concerns: OSM community label 'Unknown / Vancouver Island & Gulf Islands' is geographically imprecise — Port Hardy is northern Vancouver Island, not the Gulf Islands; no impact on listing quality.
Website contact page contains Lorem Ipsum placeholder text in the FAQ accordion, suggesting the site may not be fully maintained.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: Legitimate 4-star hotel at a key northern Vancouver Island cycling terminus, but neither required criterion (secure bike storage, staff bike procedure knowledge) is confirmed by the website. Outreach to the property is needed before a WWC listing can be justified.
enrichment_extras.notes: Port Hardy is the terminus of Highway 19 and the BC Ferries Inside Passage route — a natural overnight stop for cyclists completing or beginning a full Vancouver Island tour. Direct follow-up on bike storage would likely yield a positive result for a hotel of this calibre.
